headline: All animals share a common ancestor—evolution branched from one origin into millions of species
universal_truth: Diversity arises from unity; differences emerge from common origins over time
fun_facts: You share about 60% of your DNA with a banana—and 85% with a mouse
All life on Earth shares the same genetic code—suggesting a single origin
The last common ancestor of all animals lived about 650 million years ago
discussion_questions: How does knowing you're related to all animals change how you see them?
What evidence shows that different species are related?
Why do related animals sometimes look so different?

hook.script: You and a butterfly share an ancestor. So do you and a fish, a worm, a sponge. Every animal on Earth—from elephants to insects—traces back to a common origin. We're all distant cousins on one enormous family tree.

cliff.script: Animals look incredibly different—how can a whale be related to a fly? What evidence convinced scientists that all animals share common ancestry?
cliff.prompt: How do we know all animals are related?

options.text: DNA comparison shows shared genetic sequences across all life—the same code, similar genes
options.response: Yes. DNA doesn't lie. All life uses the same genetic language. Shared sequences reveal shared ancestry—even between very different creatures.

options.text: Similar body structures suggest common ancestors that evolved differently
options.response: Anatomy helps, but DNA provides the definitive proof of common ancestry...

fact1.title: One Code
fact1.script: All life uses the same genetic code—DNA with the same four letters, the same way of encoding proteins. This shared language strongly suggests all life descended from one original organism. Different species, same underlying programming.

fact2.title: DNA Comparison
fact2.script: Compare DNA and you find surprising similarities. Humans and chimps share 98.8% of DNA. Humans and mice share 85%. Even humans and bananas share 60%. The more similar the DNA, the more recent the common ancestor.

fact3.title: Branching Tree
fact3.script: Evolution is a branching tree, not a ladder. Species split and split again over millions of years. Every branch connects back eventually to a single trunk—one ancestor from which all animal life diversified.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Diversity arises from unity. All animal variety—millions of species—branched from common origins. We're related to every creature. That connection changes how we might see the natural world.

outro.script: That's Day 135. Tomorrow, we'll explore why we keep pets. Until then, look at an animal and consider: we share ancestors. We're family.

growTrack.title: Family Recognition - See the Connection
growTrack.activity: Next time you see an animal—any animal—remember you share ancestors. How many generations back? Millions. But the connection is real. Does knowing this change how you see that bird, that dog, that insect?
